name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield 5.21% and 30-year 5.64% on 10 Nov, lower on the month but still near multi-decade highs
state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.21% on 10 Nov, 23bp lower over the month and 82bp higher over the year; the 30-year yield was 5.64%, 28bp lower on the month (Trading Economics). Yields rose on 10 Nov with US Treasuries after US inflation data, and a Bank of England Deputy Governor flagged possible further rate rises. The 30-year yield remains near multi-decade highs and no weak auction or intervention was found, so Watch is kept rather than moving to Normal.
for_you: Gilt yields set the cost of government borrowing and influence fixed mortgage pricing and annuity rates. Pension schemes and those remortgaging are most exposed to swings.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt 5.64% near multi-decade highs (Watch); 10y 1m move -23bp, under 40bp
why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
